globalConstraints.text: Preserve generalized-role versus concrete-realization discipline. `DOKĄD`, `SKĄD`, and `GDZIE` are not new architecture types or proof of exclusive preposition government.
Keep alternative schemas alternative; never reconstruct an unsupported maximal frame.
Preserve lexical `się` and `sobie` as part of the verified identity.
Preserve required lexical `udział` in `brać udział w + Locative` and `wziąć udział w + Locative`.
Never transfer syntax through an aspect metadata relationship.
Keep ordinary Genitive under negation grammar-owned rather than creating a lemma-specific lexical pattern.
Preserve exact clause distinctions: `że`, `żeby`, interrogative-dependent, and direct speech.
Keep related identities separate, including `radzić / radzić sobie`, `uczyć / uczyć się`, and reflexive/non-reflexive entries.
Do not restore any rejected Phase 2 hypothesis during authoring.
Allocate no stable ID until the exact Phase 4 editorial record is approved under the later ID policy.

bindingConstraints.text: Author only the production sense with nad + Instrumental. Do not encode jako + Nominative or ordinary workplace GDZIE as a verb pattern.

meanings.internalScope: Goal-directed work on creating or producing something. Excludes employment, occupation, workplace, beneficiary, collaboration, and work-with-person readings.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For creating or developing something, use nad + Instrumental: pracuję nad filmem (I'm working on a film).

examples.en: I am working on a new film.

bindingConstraints.text: The locked product can encode individual do/na realizations but not the generalized DOKĄD alternation as one abstract slot; later authoring must avoid implying exclusive government.

meanings.internalScope: Directed motion on foot, including going in order to perform an action. The destination forms are individual realizations of a selected destination role, not an exhaustive government list.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For this journey on foot, do + Genitive is one common way to name the destination; other destinations use other prepositions.
For this journey on foot, na + Accusative is another way to name the destination; it does not replace other destination prepositions.
Use an infinitive to say the action you are going to do: idę kupić chleb (I'm going to buy bread).

examples.en: I am going to the shop.
I am going to the swimming pool.
I am going to buy bread.

bindingConstraints.text: The semantic boundary between event attendance na CO and a spatial na-destination must be enforced during later sense selection.

meanings.internalScope: Habitual attendance at an activity or institution. The na + Accusative pattern is for the activity or attendance reading, not a merely spatial na-destination.
Repeated or habitual motion on foot to a place or in order to do an action. Keeps the selected destination and infinitive purpose separate from attendance/activity na + Accusative.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For a regular activity or class, use na + Accusative: chodzę na kurs polskiego (I go to a Polish course). This is not just a spatial destination.
For regular trips on foot, do + Genitive can name a selected destination; other destination prepositions are possible in other contexts.
Use an infinitive to say the activity you go to do regularly: chodzę pływać (I go swimming).

examples.en: I go to a Polish course.
I go to the library regularly.
I go swimming.

bindingConstraints.text: Walenty could not be inspected at lemma level, so the unexpected selected-vehicle result lacks independent corroboration and deserves reviewer attention.

meanings.internalScope: Directed travel using a vehicle, animal, or transport or sport equipment. Destination and selected vehicle/equipment constructions are separate patterns; route, time, and ordinary manner are excluded.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For this journey by transport, do + Genitive is one way to name the selected destination; it is not the only possible destination preposition.
When you name the vehicle, use the bare Instrumental: jadę autobusem (I'm travelling by bus). In this sense it names the selected vehicle for the journey.
Use na + Locative for travel on a vehicle or piece of equipment: jadę na rowerze (I'm travelling by bicycle).

examples.en: I am travelling to Gdańsk.
I am travelling by bus.
I am travelling by bicycle.

bindingConstraints.text: As with jechać, independent lemma-level Walenty corroboration was unavailable; exact pedagogical delimitation of vehicle participant versus manner needs review.

meanings.internalScope: Repeated or habitual overland travel using transport. Frequency is part of the meaning but is not a complement; destination and selected vehicle/equipment constructions are separate patterns.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For repeated travel by transport, do + Genitive can name a selected destination; other destination prepositions are possible in other contexts.
When you name the vehicle for repeated travel, use the bare Instrumental: jeżdżę tramwajem (I travel by tram). This is a selected vehicle pattern, not a frequency pattern.
Use na + Locative for repeated travel on a vehicle or piece of equipment: jeżdżę na nartach (I go skiing).

examples.en: I travel to Gdynia.
I travel by tram.
I go skiing.

glossesEn: arrive at a truth or conviction
meanings.internalScope: The abstract intellectual-result sense of reaching a thought, truth, conclusion, or conviction. Excludes literal walking destinations and other dojść senses.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For reaching a conclusion or truth, use do + Genitive: dojść do wniosku (reach a conclusion). This is not about physically walking somewhere.

examples.en: We reached a conclusion.

bindingConstraints.text: The selected-vehicle analysis should receive independent review because it reverses the Phase 2 working suspicion and Walenty was inaccessible.

glossesEn: get to a destination by vehicle
meanings.internalScope: Reaching an endpoint through travel in or on transport. Concrete do and na endpoint forms are individual realizations of the selected endpoint role; vehicle and equipment constructions remain separate.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For reaching an endpoint by transport, do + Genitive is one way to name it; it is not the only possible endpoint preposition.
For reaching an endpoint by transport, na + Accusative is another way to name it; other endpoint prepositions are possible.
When you name the vehicle used to reach the endpoint, use the bare Instrumental: dojadę pociągiem (I'll get there by train).
Use na + Locative for reaching the endpoint on a vehicle or piece of equipment: dojedziemy na rowerach (we'll get there by bicycle).

examples.en: We will get to the hotel.
We will get to the station.
I will get there by train.
We will get there by bicycle.

bindingConstraints.text: Label do/z forms as goal/source realizations, never as exclusive government; keep the imperfective evidence independent from wrócić.

meanings.internalScope: Imperfective return to a place previously occupied. The do and z forms are concrete realizations of selected return-goal and return-source positions, not exclusive government.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For this return meaning, do + Genitive can express the place you return to. It is one realization of the return goal, not the only form.
For this return meaning, z + Genitive can express the place you return from. It is one realization of the return source, not the only form.

examples.en: I am returning to the flat.
I am coming back from the cinema.

bindingConstraints.text: Label do/z as realizations, preserve the moderate independent-slot signal, and do not inherit syntax from wracać.

meanings.internalScope: Bounded perfective return to a place previously occupied. This independently evidenced meaning uses concrete do and z realizations of selected return-goal and return-source positions, not exclusive government.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For this completed return, do + Genitive can express the place you return to. It is one realization of the return goal, not the only form.
For this completed return, z + Genitive can express the place you return from. It is one realization of the return source, not the only form.

examples.en: I will return to the flat.
I came back from the cinema.

bindingConstraints.text: Keep event/activity and place readings sense-specific; label concrete destinations as realizations and do not author an unverified person-target do frame.

meanings.internalScope: Literal arrival at a place. The do + Genitive form is a concrete realization of a selected destination role; this record excludes person-specific targets.
One-off arrival in order to perform or undergo an activity or event. Keeps event/activity na + Accusative and the selected infinitive separate from literal place arrival and arrival time.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For literal arrival at a place, do + Genitive can name the destination; it is one way to express that destination.
For a one-off event or activity, na + Accusative can name the destination: przyszliśmy na koncert (we came to a concert).
Use an infinitive to say the one-off action you came to do: przyszedłem odebrać dokument (I came to collect a document).

examples.en: We came to the museum.
We came to a concert.
I came to collect a document.

bindingConstraints.text: Author do/na only as destination realizations, not exclusive government; exclude source, vehicle, route, and time from the lexical pattern.

meanings.internalScope: Arrival at a destination by travelling in or on transport. do+Genitive and na+Accusative are individual realizations of a selected destination role, not exhaustive government. Excludes source, vehicle, route, time, and manner; no syntax is borrowed from imperfective przyjeżdżać.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: One common way to express this destination is do + Genitive: przyjadę do Warszawy (I'll arrive in Warsaw).
Another common way to express this destination is na + Accusative: przyjadę na dworzec (I'll arrive at the station).

examples.en: I will arrive in Warsaw.
I will arrive at the station.

bindingConstraints.text: Keep literal exit separate from sport/result meanings and label every concrete source/destination form as a generalized-role realization.

meanings.internalScope: Literal exit from a bounded place. z+Genitive realizes a selected source role; do+Genitive and na+Accusative realize a selected destination role. All are non-exclusive realizations. Excludes the separately evidenced ranking/result sense (na+Accusative, e.g. 'wyjść na prowadzenie'), which is not authored in this record; also excludes route, time, and manner. No syntax is borrowed from imperfective wychodzić.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: One common way to say where you're leaving from is z + Genitive: wyszedłem z domu (I left the house). This is a common realization of the source, not the only possible form.
One common way to name where you're going after leaving is do + Genitive: wyjdę do ogrodu (I'll go out to the garden).
Another common way to name that destination is na + Accusative: wyjdę na balkon (I'll go out onto the balcony).

examples.en: I left the house.
I will go out to the garden.
I will go out onto the balcony.

bindingConstraints.text: Author only the source-role realization; do not add destination, vehicle, route, or time frames and do not imply exclusive z government.

glossesEn: depart from a place by vehicle
meanings.internalScope: Leaving a bounded area by transport. z+Genitive realizes a selected source role, not exclusive government. Excludes destination, vehicle, route, time, and manner. No syntax is borrowed from imperfective wyjeżdżać.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: One common way to say where you're leaving from by transport is z + Genitive: wyjadę z miasta (I'll leave the city). This is a common realization of the source, not the only possible form. It does not name a destination.

examples.en: I will leave the city.

bindingConstraints.text: Keep the exact imperfective identity and Accusative object; do not author a Dative recipient or inherit any construction from przynieść.

meanings.internalScope: Physically carrying or bringing a thing to a destination. Direct Accusative names the carried object. Optional generalized source/goal roles exist in the sense but no concrete preposition realization is authored for product use. No Dative recipient exists; that Phase 2 hypothesis was explicitly rejected. No syntax is inherited from perfective przynieść.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The thing you bring takes the Accusative: przynoszę kawę (I'm bringing coffee).

examples.en: I am bringing coffee.

bindingConstraints.text: Author the exact answer sense with alternative na-question and że-content schemas; exclude an unverified Dative person and unrelated meanings.

meanings.internalScope: Answering a question or prior utterance by speaking. na+Accusative names the question/content target; że introduces a content clause; direct speech may also express the answer's content. These are alternatives, not a combined maximal frame. No Dative addressee exists; the person spoken to is not a schema position. Matching/preference, correspondence, and other odpowiadać senses are excluded.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For what you're answering, use na + Accusative: odpowiadam na pytanie (I'm answering the question).
Use że to introduce the content of your answer: odpowiadam, że nie wiem (I answer that I don't know).
You can also give the answer's exact words directly: odpowiadam: „Nie wiem” (I answer: "I don't know").

examples.en: I am answering the question.
I answer that I don't know.
I answer: "I don't know."

bindingConstraints.text: Keep beneficiary schemas alternative, label u + Genitive as a realization rather than exclusive provider government, and do not build a maximal frame.

meanings.internalScope: Ordering or commissioning something for payment. Accusative names the ordered item. Dative and dla+Genitive are alternative beneficiary realizations of the same participant, not combined into one frame. u+Genitive is a documented realization of a selected provider/location role, not exclusive provider government. No syntax is borrowed from perfective zamówić.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The thing you order takes the Accusative: zamawiam pizzę (I'm ordering a pizza).
To say who the order is for, one way is the Dative: zamawiam mężowi prezent (I'm ordering a present for my husband).
Another way to say who the order is for is dla + Genitive: zamawiam prezent dla żony (I'm ordering a present for my wife).
One common way to name the provider is u + Genitive: zamawiam meble u stolarza (I'm ordering furniture from a carpenter).

examples.en: I am ordering a pizza.
I am ordering a present for my husband.
I am ordering a present for my wife.
I am ordering furniture from a carpenter.

meanings.internalScope: Bounded onset of an activity. Accusative names the activity as a direct object; infinitive names the action begun. Both are independently evidenced for perfective zacząć; no syntax is inherited from the metadata-only imperfective partner zaczynać.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The activity you start takes the Accusative: zacząłem lekcję (I started the lesson).
Use an infinitive to say what you started doing: zacząłem czytać książkę (I started reading a book).

examples.en: I started the lesson.
I started reading a book.

meanings.internalScope: Bringing an activity or task to its end. Accusative names the activity/task; the infinitive is selected, naming the action being finished, not a purpose adjunct. Exact imperfective kończyć is independently evidenced; no syntax is borrowed from perfective skończyć, and this record does not pre-decide the later kończyć/skończyć pair policy.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The task you finish takes the Accusative: kończę pracę (I'm finishing the work).
Use an infinitive to say what you're finishing doing: kończę czytać książkę (I'm finishing reading the book).

examples.en: I am finishing the work.
I am finishing reading the book.

meanings.internalScope: Recalling or retaining people, things, events, or information. Direct Accusative names the remembered person/thing/event/information; o+Locative names a remembered topic. Independently verified że-content-clause and interrogative-dependent-clause constructions also exist in this exact sense but are intentionally not authored in this record; see the Batch 2 risk report for the omission rationale. Excludes the distinct obligation/reminder meaning and does not use żeby.

Remembering that an action should be performed; an obligation/reminder sense distinct from ordinary recall. Infinitive and żeby-clause are both selected. Not merged into recall merely because English can translate both with 'remember'; does not use że or o+Locative.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The thing you remember takes the Accusative: pamiętam ten dzień (I remember that day).
For a remembered topic, use o + Locative: pamiętam o twoich urodzinach (I remember your birthday).
Use an infinitive when you and the person doing the action are the same: pamiętaj zamknąć drzwi (remember to close the door).
Use żeby when the person who should act is different: pamiętaj, żeby dzieci umyły ręce (remember that the children should wash their hands).

examples.en: I remember that day.
I remember your birthday.
Remember to close the door.
Remember that the children should wash their hands.

bindingConstraints.text: Keep recall and failure-to-act senses separate and omit the unverified żeby schema.

meanings.internalScope: Losing recall of people, things, events, or information. Direct Genitive and direct Accusative both realize the remembered/forgotten object; o+Locative names a remembered topic; że and czy content clauses realize forgotten propositional/question content. All are directly verified for this exact sense. Excludes the distinct failure-to-act meaning below and does not use żeby; that schema was explicitly rejected by Phase 3.

glossesEn: fail to do something one should have done
meanings.internalScope: Failing to perform an action that should have been performed. Infinitive is the sole authorized construction. The proposed żeby-clause was explicitly rejected by Phase 3 evidence and must not be authored here. No syntax is inherited from another aspect identity; this meaning is kept separate from the recall/forgetting sense above.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The forgotten thing can take the Genitive: zapominam numeru telefonu (I forget the phone number).
The forgotten thing can also take the Accusative: zapominam tę twarz (I forget that face).
For a forgotten topic, use o + Locative: zapominam o spotkaniu (I forget about the meeting).
Use że to introduce what you forget: zapominam, że mam spotkanie (I forget that I have a meeting).
Use czy to introduce a forgotten yes/no question: zapominam, czy zamknąłem drzwi (I forget whether I locked the door).
Use an infinitive to say the action you failed to do: zapominam zadzwonić (I forget to call).

examples.en: I forget the phone number.
I forget that face.
I forget about the meeting.
I forget that I have a meeting.
I forget whether I locked the door.
I forget to call.

meanings.internalScope: Attempting an action or result. The infinitive names the attempted action; a direct Genitive action noun (a noun, not an infinitive) names the attempted result. Both belong to this exact sense, retained under the completeness rule.

Checking the taste of food or drink. Direct Genitive names the sampled object. Shares surface case with the attempt sense's Genitive action noun but is a materially different meaning; the two are not merged. Purpose, manner, time, and other tasting circumstances are not complements.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: Use an infinitive to say what you're trying to do: próbuję rozwiązać problem (I'm trying to solve the problem).
The attempted result can also be a noun in the Genitive: próbuję szczęścia (I'm trying my luck).
The food or drink you taste takes the Genitive: próbuję zupy (I'm tasting the soup).

examples.en: I'm trying to solve the problem.
I'm trying my luck.
I'm tasting the soup.

bindingConstraints.text: Author the listed alternative schemas separately; do not freely combine Dative, na + Accusative, infinitive, and żeby positions or transfer participants across senses.

meanings.internalScope: Human permission or non-prevention. Optional Dative names the permitted person; it belongs only to the na + Accusative and żeby-clause variants below, never to the standalone infinitive. Do not combine Dative with the infinitive. No syntax is inherited from perfective pozwolić.

An inanimate thing or situation enabling an action or result. No Dative participant exists in this sense; it is never transferred from the human-permission sense above. na + Accusative, infinitive, and żeby-clause remain independent alternatives here, not one combined frame.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: You can name who is allowed with the Dative, then say what with na + Accusative: mama pozwala mi na wyjście (Mom allows me to go out).
Use żeby when the permitted person is the subject of their own clause: mama pozwala, żeby dzieci oglądały bajki (Mom allows the children to watch cartoons).
A standalone infinitive gives general permission without naming a person: pozwalam pracować z domu (I allow working from home).
For a thing or situation making something possible, use na + Accusative: internet pozwala na szybką komunikację (the internet allows quick communication).
An infinitive can also follow directly: internet pozwala pracować zdalnie (the internet allows working remotely).
A żeby-clause can follow when the enabling thing is more abstract, such as a law or policy: prawo pozwala, żeby firmy stosowały ulgi (the law allows companies to apply tax breaks).

examples.en: Mom allows me to go out.

examples.pl: Mama pozwala, żeby dzieci oglądały bajki.
examples.en: Mom allows the children to watch cartoons.
I allow working from home.
The internet allows quick communication.
The internet allows working remotely.

examples.pl: Prawo pozwala, żeby firmy stosowały ulgi.
examples.en: The law allows companies to apply tax breaks.

bindingConstraints.text: Author direct Genitive only and omit infinitive government.

meanings.internalScope: Trying not to experience, participate in, do, or contact the object. Direct Genitive is the sole authorized construction. Infinitive government was explicitly rejected by Phase 3 and is not authored; a Genitive gerund/action noun remains a noun in Genitive, not an infinitive complement.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The thing you avoid takes the Genitive: unikam słodyczy (I avoid sweets).

examples.en: I avoid sweets.

glossesEn: require conduct or a trait from someone
meanings.internalScope: A person requiring conduct or a trait. Genitive names the required content; optional od + Genitive names the person the requirement is directed at; żeby introduces a clause. The optional od participant here is restricted to a person, unlike the situation-requires meaning below. od + Genitive is directly selected by this schema, not a narrowed realization of a generalized role. There is no standalone od + Genitive construction; od only appears optionally alongside the required Genitive or żeby complement.

glossesEn: make conduct or a condition necessary
meanings.internalScope: A situation making conduct or a condition necessary. Genitive names the required content; optional od + Genitive names the person or thing the requirement is directed at (broader than the person-only restriction above); żeby introduces a clause. Not merged with the person-requires meaning despite the shared surface forms. There is no standalone od + Genitive construction; od only appears optionally alongside the required Genitive or żeby complement.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The required thing takes the Genitive; you can optionally add od + Genitive for the person it's required from: wymaga lojalności od pracowników (it requires loyalty from employees).

Use żeby to introduce what someone is required to do; you can optionally add od + Genitive for the person it applies to: szef wymaga, żeby pracownicy przychodzili punktualnie (the boss requires that employees arrive on time).

The required thing takes the Genitive; you can optionally add od + Genitive for the person or thing it's required from: wyjście z nałogu wymaga silnej woli (getting out of an addiction requires strong will).

A żeby-clause can follow when the requiring subject is an abstract situation; you can optionally add od + Genitive for the person or thing it applies to: sytuacja wymaga, żeby wszyscy zachowali spokój (the situation requires that everyone stay calm).

examples.en: It requires loyalty from employees.

examples.pl: Szef wymaga, żeby pracownicy przychodzili punktualnie.
examples.en: The boss requires that employees arrive on time.

examples.pl: Wyjście z nałogu wymaga silnej woli.
examples.en: Getting out of an addiction requires strong will.

examples.pl: Sytuacja wymaga, żeby wszyscy zachowali spokój.
examples.en: The situation requires that everyone stay calm.

meanings.internalScope: Being owned by a person or group. do + Genitive names the owner. This is an exact schema, not a narrowed generalized-role realization. Category, relationship, obligation, należeć się, location, time, and manner are not imported.

glossesEn: be a member of a group or organization
meanings.internalScope: Being a member of an organization or group. do + Genitive names the organization/group. Shares the same surface do + Genitive form as ownership above but is a distinct, separately evidenced meaning; the two are kept apart rather than flattened into one generic 'belong to' record.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For who owns something, use do + Genitive: ten dom należy do sąsiadki (this house belongs to my neighbor).
For the group you belong to, use do + Genitive: należę do klubu sportowego (I belong to a sports club).

examples.en: This house belongs to my neighbor.
I belong to a sports club.

meanings.internalScope: Lexical-reflexive interpersonal quarrelling; się is part of the identity and nothing is transferred from non-reflexive kłócić. For a singular personal subject, z + Instrumental names the interlocutor and o + Accusative names the topic, each independently. A plural reciprocal subject naturally omits a separate z-interlocutor. że and the interrogative clause are alternatives to the nominal o + Accusative topic, not to the interlocutor. Frequency, intensity, manner, place, and other circumstances are not complements.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For who you're arguing with, use z + Instrumental: kłócę się z bratem (I argue with my brother).
For the topic of the argument, use o + Accusative: kłócimy się o drobiazgi (we argue about trivial things). A plural subject like this doesn't need a separate z-phrase.
Use że to introduce the topic as a clause: kłócimy się, że nikt nie sprząta (we argue that nobody cleans up).
Use czy to introduce an undecided yes/no topic: kłócimy się, czy powinniśmy wyjechać (we're arguing about whether we should leave).

examples.en: I argue with my brother.
We argue about trivial things.

examples.pl: Kłócimy się, że nikt nie sprząta.
examples.en: We argue that nobody cleans up.
We're arguing about whether we should leave.

meanings.internalScope: Directing a person's attention so that a person, thing, place, or content is seen. Optional Dative names the recipient and Accusative names the thing shown, in one schema. A separate exact na + Accusative names what is pointed at/toward, distinct from the Dative+Accusative showing frame. An interrogative-dependent clause names shown content. Optional GDZIE also occurs in the evidence as selected semantic-role evidence only; it is not concretized into any w/na + Locative or other location pattern. No syntax is borrowed from pokazać.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The person you show something to takes the Dative, and the thing shown takes the Accusative: pokazuję dzieciom zdjęcia (I'm showing the children photos).
To point at or toward something, use na + Accusative: pokazuję na mapę (I'm pointing at the map).
Use a question word to introduce shown content: pokazuję, jak to zrobić (I show how to do it).

examples.en: I'm showing the children photos.
I'm pointing at the map.
I show how to do it.

phase3Evidence.primarySourceLocator: single lexical entry; Definicja, Połączenia, Składnia

meanings.internalScope: Overcoming or managing difficulties independently. sobie is part of the lexical identity, not a free Dative complement. Optional z + Instrumental names the difficulty. Situational w-phrases and other forms shown only in connections receive no frame credit. Nothing is transferred from non-reflexive advice-sense radzić; both are intentionally retained as distinct full lemmas.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For the difficulty you're handling, use z + Instrumental: radzę sobie z trudnościami (I cope with difficulties).

examples.en: I cope with difficulties.

meanings.internalScope: Imperfective process, habitual, or repeated buying. Accusative names the purchased goods in every schema. Schema A adds optional od + Genitive seller and optional za + Accusative price together; schema B adds an optional Dative beneficiary; schema C adds an optional dla + Genitive beneficiary. The three schemas are alternatives, not one maximal purchase frame. Purchase location, channel, occasion, frequency, and manner remain outside the pattern inventory. No syntax is inherited from perfective kupić.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: You can add who you buy from with od + Genitive and the price with za + Accusative: kupuję warzywa od rolnika za dziesięć złotych (I buy vegetables from a farmer for ten złoty).
To say who benefits, one way is the Dative: kupuję dzieciom zabawki (I buy the children toys).
Another way to say who benefits is dla + Genitive: kupuję zabawki dla dzieci (I buy toys for the children).

examples.pl: Kupuję warzywa od rolnika za dziesięć złotych.
examples.en: I buy vegetables from a farmer for ten złoty.
I buy the children toys.
I buy toys for the children.

meanings.internalScope: Perfective bounded acquisition of goods for money. Accusative names the purchased goods in every schema. Schema A adds optional od + Genitive seller and optional za + Accusative price together; schema B adds an optional Dative beneficiary; schema C adds an optional dla + Genitive beneficiary. The three schemas are alternatives, not one maximal purchase frame. Dative is not generalized to every purchase context. Purchase place, channel, occasion, frequency, manner, and means of payment are not promoted. Independently evidenced from imperfective kupować; no construction is unique against kupować's inventory, but no syntax is inherited from it either.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: You can add who you bought from with od + Genitive and the price with za + Accusative: kupię chleb od piekarza za pięć złotych (I will buy bread from a baker for five złoty).
To say who benefits, one way is the Dative: kupiłem jej kwiaty (I bought her flowers).
Another way to say who benefits is dla + Genitive: kupiłem prezenty dla całej rodziny (I bought presents for the whole family).

examples.pl: Kupię chleb od piekarza za pięć złotych.
examples.en: I will buy bread from a baker for five złoty.
I bought her flowers.
I bought presents for the whole family.

meanings.internalScope: Imperfective transfer causing a recipient to own or use a thing; process, repeated, and habitual transfer. Accusative object and Dative recipient are both required in the same schema. Gift occasion, purpose, manner, time, and w prezencie-style contextual gift language are not complements.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The thing given takes the Accusative and the recipient takes the Dative, and both are required: daję sąsiadowi klucze (I'm giving the neighbor the keys).

examples.en: I'm giving the neighbor the keys.

meanings.internalScope: Completed/bounded transfer causing a recipient to own or use a thing, independently evidenced from dawać. Accusative object and Dative recipient are both required. Gift occasion, purpose, manner, time, and w prezencie-style language are not complements.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The thing given takes the Accusative and the recipient takes the Dative, and both are required: dałem sąsiadowi klucze (I gave the neighbor the keys).

examples.en: I gave the neighbor the keys.

meanings.internalScope: Literal grasping/taking of an entity. Two distinct source schemas are kept as alternatives: an Accusative object with an optional Instrumental means (animate subject), and an Accusative object with a required za + Accusative gripped part (personal subject). Destination, manner, time, and circumstance are not complements.

Fixed lexical construction brać udział w czymś = participation, a separate lexical entry, not derived from ordinary object syntax. udział is required lexical material of the fixed construction, not a replaceable Accusative object; the schema structurally encodes only w + Locative. A personal subject is required. Participation modifiers, event circumstances, time, and manner are not complements, and this is never modelled as generic brać + w + Locative.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The thing taken takes the Accusative; you can optionally add the Instrumental for what it's taken with: biorę kostki lodu szczypcami (I pick up ice cubes with tongs).
To take hold of someone or something by a part, use Accusative + za + Accusative for the gripped part, both required: biorę dziecko za rękę (I'm taking the child by the hand).

brać udział w + Locative is a fixed expression meaning to take part in something; udział is a fixed word here, not a replaceable object: biorę udział w konferencji (I'm taking part in the conference).

examples.en: I pick up ice cubes with tongs.
I'm taking the child by the hand.
I'm taking part in the conference.

meanings.internalScope: Bounded literal grasping/taking, independently evidenced from brać. Same two alternatives: Accusative with optional Instrumental means (animate subject), and Accusative with required za + Accusative gripped part (personal subject). Destination, time, manner, and circumstance are not complements.

Fixed lexical construction wziąć udział w czymś = entry into participation, a separate WSJP fixed entry, independently evidenced from brać's. udział is required lexical material, not a replaceable object; only w + Locative is structurally encoded. A personal subject is required. Participation modifiers, event circumstances, time, and manner are not complements.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The thing taken takes the Accusative; you can optionally add the Instrumental for what it's taken with: wziąłem kostkę lodu szczypcami (I picked up an ice cube with tongs).
To take hold of someone or something by a part, use Accusative + za + Accusative for the gripped part, both required: wziąłem dziecko za rękę (I took the child by the hand).

wziąć udział w + Locative is a fixed expression meaning to enter into participation; udział is a fixed word here, not a replaceable object: wziąłem udział w konferencji (I took part in the conference).

examples.en: I picked up an ice cube with tongs.
I took the child by the hand.
I took part in the conference.

meanings.internalScope: Reading written symbols/text, including process/habitual reading, content reporting, and reading aloud. Five alternatives: bare Accusative content with an optional Dative listener; a required o + Locative topic with optional Accusative and Dative; a że-clause or interrogative-dependent clause each with an optional o + Locative topic; and direct speech with an optional Dative listener. Reading frequency, speed, manner, language, medium, and incidental place are not complements, and no concrete location frame (w/na + Locative, do + Genitive, or any other location preposition) is ever authored from the generalized GDZIE evidence.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: What is read takes the Accusative; you can optionally add the Dative for who it's read to: czytam dzieciom książkę (I'm reading the children a book).
To read about a topic, use o + Locative, which is required here: czytam o polityce (I'm reading about politics). This names the topic you're reading about, not a location.
Use że to introduce what you read as a clause: czytam, że ceny rosną (I'm reading that prices are rising).
Use a question word to introduce read content: czytam, dlaczego ceny rosną (I'm reading why prices are rising).
You can also read exact words aloud directly, optionally naming who you're reading to with the Dative: czytam dzieciom: „Ala ma kota” (I'm reading to the children: "Ala has a cat.").

examples.en: I'm reading the children a book.
I'm reading about politics.
I'm reading that prices are rising.
I'm reading why prices are rising.
I'm reading to the children: "Ala has a cat."

meanings.internalScope: Creating and recording a text or music (WSJP sense 2). Bare Accusative names the created text; no addressee. Correspondence addressees of any form, writing medium, place, time, language, frequency, and manner are not complements, and creative-sense do + Genitive newspaper connections are not modelled as an addressee schema.

Communicating information in writing (WSJP sense 4). Six content families (o + Locative topic, że-clause, żeby-clause, interrogative-dependent clause, direct speech, bare Accusative content) each optionally take a recipient in one of two mutually exclusive alternative forms, Dative or do + Genitive. Every recipient is optional in every pisać correspondence schema; Dative and do + Genitive never co-occur in one pattern. Writing medium, place, time, language, frequency, and manner are not complements, and do + Genitive is never generalized beyond correspondence.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: What you write takes the Accusative: piszę powieść (I'm writing a novel).

For the topic you're writing about, use o + Locative, which is required here; you can optionally add the Dative for who you're writing to (no preposition): piszę koledze o wakacjach (I'm writing my friend about the holidays).

Use że to introduce what you're writing as a clause; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you're writing to: piszę koledze, że wracam jutro (I'm writing to my friend that I'll be back tomorrow).
Use żeby to introduce what you're asking someone to do; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you're writing to: piszę koledze, żeby zadzwonił (I'm writing my friend, asking him to call).
Use a question word to introduce written content; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you're writing to: piszę koledze, o której wrócę (I'm writing to my friend what time I'll be back).
You can write exact words directly; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you're writing to: piszę koledze: „Wracam jutro” (I'm writing to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow.").
What you write takes the Accusative; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you're writing to: piszę koledze wiadomość (I'm writing my friend a message).

For the topic you're writing about, use o + Locative, which is required here; you can optionally add do + Genitive (literally 'to') for who you're writing to: piszę do koleżanki o wakacjach (I'm writing to my friend about the holidays).

Use że to introduce what you're writing as a clause; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you're writing to: piszę do koleżanki, że wracam jutro (I'm writing to my friend that I'm coming back tomorrow).

Use żeby to introduce what you're asking someone to do; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you're writing to: piszę do koleżanki, żeby zadzwoniła (I'm writing to my friend, asking her to call).
Use a question word to introduce written content; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you're writing to: piszę do koleżanki, o której wrócę (I'm writing to my friend what time I'll be back).
You can write exact words directly; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you're writing to: piszę do koleżanki: „Wracam jutro” (I'm writing to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow.").
What you write takes the Accusative; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you're writing to: piszę do koleżanki wiadomość (I'm writing a message to my friend).

examples.en: I'm writing a novel.
I'm writing my friend about the holidays.
I'm writing to my friend that I'll be back tomorrow.
I'm writing my friend, asking him to call.
I'm writing to my friend what time I'll be back.
I'm writing to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow."
I'm writing my friend a message.
I'm writing to my friend about the holidays.

examples.pl: Piszę do koleżanki, że wracam jutro.
examples.en: I'm writing to my friend that I'm coming back tomorrow.
I'm writing to my friend, asking her to call.

examples.pl: Piszę do koleżanki, o której wrócę.
examples.en: I'm writing to my friend what time I'll be back.
I'm writing to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow."
I'm writing a message to my friend.

meanings.internalScope: Completed creation and recording of a text or music (WSJP sense 2), independently evidenced from pisać. Bare Accusative names the created text; no addressee. Correspondence addressees, medium, place, time, language, repetition, and manner are not complements, and creative-sense do + Genitive newspaper connections are not modelled as an addressee schema.

Completed written communication (WSJP sense 4), independently evidenced from pisać. Same six content families, each taking a recipient in one of two mutually exclusive alternative forms, Dative or do + Genitive. Critical asymmetry: Dative is required on exactly the three clause alternatives (że, żeby, interrogative-dependent) and optional on topic, direct speech, and bare Accusative content; do + Genitive remains optional throughout. This schema-specific requiredness is preserved exactly and is never normalized to pisać's uniformly-optional Dative in either direction. Medium, place, time, language, repetition, and manner are not complements.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: What you write takes the Accusative: napisałem powieść (I wrote a novel).

For the topic you're writing about, use o + Locative, which is required here; the bare Dative recipient is optional in this alternative: napisałem koledze o wakacjach (I wrote my friend about the holidays).

Use że to introduce what you wrote as a clause. Unlike pisać, in this clause alternative the bare Dative recipient is REQUIRED, not optional: napisałem koledze, że wrócę jutro (I wrote to my friend that I'll be back tomorrow).
Use żeby to introduce what you're asking someone to do. The bare Dative recipient is REQUIRED in this clause alternative: napisałem koledze, żeby zadzwonił (I wrote my friend, asking him to call).
Use a question word to introduce written content. The bare Dative recipient is REQUIRED in this clause alternative: napisałem koledze, o której wrócę (I wrote to my friend what time I'll be back).
You can write exact words directly; the bare Dative recipient is optional here: napisałem koledze: „Wracam jutro” (I wrote to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow.").
What you write takes the Accusative; the bare Dative recipient is optional here: napisałem koledze wiadomość (I wrote my friend a message).

For the topic you're writing about, use o + Locative, which is required here; do + Genitive for the recipient stays optional throughout, unlike Dative on the clause alternatives: napisałem do koleżanki o wakacjach (I wrote to my friend about the holidays).
Use że to introduce what you wrote as a clause; do + Genitive for the recipient remains optional here: napisałem do koleżanki, że wracam jutro (I wrote to my friend that I'm coming back tomorrow).
Use żeby to introduce what you're asking someone to do; do + Genitive for the recipient remains optional here: napisałem do koleżanki, żeby zadzwoniła (I wrote to my friend, asking her to call).
Use a question word to introduce written content; do + Genitive for the recipient remains optional here: napisałem do koleżanki, o której wrócę (I wrote to my friend what time I'll be back).
You can write exact words directly; do + Genitive for the recipient remains optional here: napisałem do koleżanki: „Wracam jutro” (I wrote to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow.").
What you write takes the Accusative; do + Genitive for the recipient remains optional here: napisałem do koleżanki wiadomość (I wrote a message to my friend).

examples.en: I wrote a novel.
I wrote my friend about the holidays.
I wrote to my friend that I'll be back tomorrow.
I wrote my friend, asking him to call.
I wrote to my friend what time I'll be back.
I wrote to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow."
I wrote my friend a message.
I wrote to my friend about the holidays.

examples.pl: Napisałem do koleżanki, że wracam jutro.
examples.en: I wrote to my friend that I'm coming back tomorrow.
I wrote to my friend, asking her to call.

examples.pl: Napisałem do koleżanki, o której wrócę.
examples.en: I wrote to my friend what time I'll be back.
I wrote to my friend: "I'm coming back tomorrow."
I wrote a message to my friend.

meanings.internalScope: Recurring or processual social meetings and contact. z + Instrumental names the meeting partner for a singular personal subject. A reciprocal plural personal subject (e.g. 'we meet') may occur without a separate partner phrase; this is a participant/usage restriction, not a second complementless pattern. się is part of the lexical identity, not a free complement. Frequency, time, place, manner, purpose, and accompanying activities are not complements.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For who you meet up with, use z + Instrumental: spotykam się z przyjaciółmi (I meet up with friends). A reciprocal plural subject like 'we meet' doesn't need a separate z-phrase.

examples.en: I meet up with friends.

meanings.internalScope: A completed/bounded social meeting or contact, independently evidenced from spotykać się (Batch 05 §41). Same z + Instrumental meeting-partner schema and the same singular/reciprocal-plural participant treatment. się is part of the lexical identity. Time, place, manner, purpose, and accompanying activities are not complements.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For who you met up with, use z + Instrumental: spotkałem się z przyjaciółmi (I met up with friends). A reciprocal plural subject like 'we met' doesn't need a separate z-phrase.

examples.en: I met up with friends.

meanings.internalScope: Processual or habitual viewing of a film, programme, performance, or other visual content (WSJP sense 2). The optional w + Locative names the presentation context in which the viewed person/content appears (e.g. the film or show they are in) — it is an exact listed position, not a realization of a generalized role, and is never generalized to ordinary viewing place, device, screen, or medium. Viewing time, frequency, and manner are not complements. Nothing is inherited from obejrzeć.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The person or content you watch takes the Accusative; you can optionally add w + Locative for the film/show they appear in — not the TV or place you're watching from: oglądam ją w nowym serialu (I'm watching her in a new series).

examples.en: I'm watching her in a new series.

glossesEn: view something all the way through
meanings.internalScope: Completed viewing resulting in acquaintance with a film, programme, performance, or other visual content (WSJP sense 2), independently evidenced from oglądać. No optional w + Locative is imported. Viewing place, medium, device, time, and manner are not complements.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: What you watched takes the Accusative: obejrzałem ten film (I watched that movie).

examples.en: I watched that movie.

meanings.internalScope: Bringing a noun- or infinitive-denoted activity to completion (WSJP sense 1). Two alternatives: bare Accusative task/activity, or an infinitive naming the completed activity. Completion time, deadline, place, manner, and result circumstances are not complements. z + Instrumental belongs only to the separate cessation meaning below and is never added here. Nothing is inherited from kończyć.
Colloquial definitive ceasing of an activity or habit (WSJP sense 4) — a separate sense, not a variant of task completion. z + Instrumental names the activity or habit being given up for good.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The finished task or activity takes the Accusative: skończyłem pracę (I finished the work).
Use an infinitive for the activity you finished doing: skończyłem pisać raport (I finished writing the report).
Use z + Instrumental for definitively giving up a habit or activity for good — a separate colloquial sense from finishing an ordinary task: skończyłem z paleniem (I'm done with smoking).

examples.en: I finished the work.
I finished writing the report.
I'm done with smoking.

meanings.internalScope: Desire for an object, one's own action, or an event/state (WSJP sense 1). The Genitive-object schema carries two optional participants, od + Genitive (source) and dla + Genitive (beneficiary), inside the same pattern. Infinitive expresses the wanting participant's own action; żeby expresses a desired event/state distinct from that action. Purpose, reason, degree, and contextual beneficiary phrases outside the exact schemas are not complements. Directly listed adverbial JAK lies outside the locked four complement types and is not represented.

First-person polite request or stated intention (WSJP sense 3), kept entirely separate from ordinary desire: this sense takes Accusative (not Genitive), has no od/dla participants, and is restricted to first-person past or conditional forms (chciałbym/chciałabym, chciałem/chciałam) — never bare present-tense chcę. This usage restriction is a control-plane fact with no field in the locked schema; every pattern below must be authored and exemplified consistently with it.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The desired thing takes the Genitive; you can optionally add od + Genitive for who it's wanted from, or dla + Genitive for who it's wanted for: chcę pomocy od brata (I want help from my brother).
Use an infinitive for what you yourself want to do: chcę zwiedzić Kraków (I want to visit Krakow).
Use żeby to say you want something to happen, done by someone or something else: chcę, żeby dzieci były szczęśliwe (I want the children to be happy).
Use the first-person conditional chciałbym/chciałabym for a polite request, with the requested thing in the Accusative — not ordinary present-tense chcę: chciałbym herbatę (I would like a tea).
Use chciałbym/chciałabym plus an infinitive for a polite stated intention: chciałbym zapytać o rezerwację (I would like to ask about a reservation).
Use chciałbym/chciałabym with żeby for a polite request directed at someone else's action: chciałbym, żebyś do mnie zadzwonił (I would like you to call me).

examples.en: I want help from my brother.
I want to visit Krakow.
I want the children to be happy.
I would like a tea.
I would like to ask about a reservation.
I would like you to call me.

meanings.internalScope: Making or creating an entity (WSJP sense 1). The Accusative names the thing created. Materials, tools, place, purpose, beneficiary, time, and manner are not complements. Not merged with the activity-performance sense below despite sharing the Accusative surface.

Performing the activity named by an adjacent noun (WSJP sense 2), e.g. doing the laundry. The Accusative names the activity, not a created entity. Individual robić + noun collocations are not promoted into separate governed frames beyond this one schema. Not merged with the creation sense above.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: The thing you make or create takes the Accusative: robię ciasto (I'm making a cake).
The named activity you perform takes the Accusative — you are not creating this thing, you are doing it: robię pranie (I'm doing the laundry).

examples.en: I'm making a cake.
I'm doing the laundry.

meanings.internalScope: Comprehending communicated or represented content (WSJP sense 1): bare Accusative content, a że-clause, or an interrogative-dependent clause (how/why/what/etc., all one clause type, never separate frames). Degree, manner, language of presentation, information source, and circumstances are not complements. No clause is transferred to the person-understanding sense below.
Empathically understanding a person (WSJP sense 4), a separate meaning from comprehending content even though both surface as Accusative. No content clause attaches here.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: What you understand takes the Accusative: rozumiem żart (I understand the joke).
Use że to introduce what you understand as a clause: rozumiem, że jesteś zmęczony (I understand that you're tired).
Use a question word to introduce understood content: rozumiem, dlaczego się spóźniłeś (I understand why you were late).
The person you empathically understand takes the Accusative: rozumiem cię jak nikt inny (I understand you like no one else).

examples.en: I understand the joke.
I understand that you're tired.
I understand why you were late.
I understand you like no one else.

bindingConstraints.text: Label w + Locative as a residence-place realization rather than exclusive government; restrict z + Instrumental to the selected co-resident role.

meanings.internalScope: Residing somewhere permanently or for a long period, optionally with a co-resident (WSJP sense 1). w + Locative is a documented residence-place realization of the generalized GDZIE role — not exclusive lexical government; na and u place forms are documented in the same source entry but are not authored as additional product frames. Optional z + Instrumental names a genuine co-resident, not incidental accompaniment. Residence duration, reason, manner, and incidental companions are not complements.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: Use w + Locative for where you live — a documented residence-place realization, not the only possible form; add z + Instrumental for a co-resident you live with: mieszkam w Warszawie z bratem (I live in Warsaw with my brother).

examples.en: I live in Warsaw with my brother.

bindingConstraints.text: Preserve lexical się, keep appointment and agreement senses separate, label do as a realization, and do not merge alternatives into a maximal frame.

meanings.internalScope: Arranging a meeting with another person (WSJP sense 1). Two source schemas: one fully optional (a partner and an appointment/event, neither forced required), and one representing a selected venue/service position through a narrowed do + Genitive realization — do + Genitive is required only in that one product row because the row exists to represent that position, never because do is exclusive government or the only possible location form. A further source-selected time position (KIEDY) has no documented concrete realization and is intentionally not represented as any complement. A reciprocal plural personal subject ("we arranged to meet") may occur without a separate partner phrase; this is a usage fact, not a second complementless pattern. się is part of canonicalLemma, never a complement.

Reaching an agreement with another person about a term, action, or proposition (WSJP sense 2), entirely separate from arranging a meeting. Five representable content alternatives (na, o, że, żeby, interrogative-dependent), each with an optional z + Instrumental partner never split into its own pattern. A sixth source-listed alternative, co do + Genitive, is verified linguistic evidence but cannot be represented in the locked schema (which accepts only single-word prepositions); it is architecture-deferred to Phase 4C, never encoded as co or do alone, and contributes no product row here. A reciprocal plural subject may occur without a separate partner phrase, recorded as usage, not a second pattern. się is part of canonicalLemma, never a complement.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: Both the meeting partner (z + Instrumental) and the appointment/event (na + Accusative) are optional and can be named together or omitted depending on context: umówiłem się z kolegą na kawę (I arranged to meet my friend for coffee).

Use do + Genitive for the venue or service you've made an appointment at — a documented realization, not the only possible location form; you can optionally add z + Instrumental for who you arranged it with: umówiłem się z żoną do lekarza (I made an appointment with my wife at the doctor's).
Use na + Accusative for the term you agreed on; you can optionally add z + Instrumental for who you agreed with: umówiłem się z szefem na podwyżkę (I agreed with my boss on a raise).
Use o + Accusative for the subject you agreed on; you can optionally add z + Instrumental for who you agreed with: umówiłem się ze sprzedawcą o cenę (I agreed with the seller on the price).

Use że to introduce what you agreed as a clause; you can optionally add z + Instrumental for who you agreed with: umówiłem się z bratem, że pomoże mi w przeprowadzce (I agreed with my brother that he'll help me move).

Use żeby to introduce an agreed action; you can optionally add z + Instrumental for who you agreed with: umówiłem się z kolegą, żeby zachować to w tajemnicy (I agreed with my friend to keep it secret).

Use a question word to introduce what was agreed; you can optionally add z + Instrumental for who you agreed with: umówiłem się z zespołem, kto za co odpowiada (I agreed with the team who's responsible for what).

examples.pl: Umówiłem się z kolegą na kawę.
examples.en: I arranged to meet my friend for coffee.

examples.pl: Umówiłem się z żoną do lekarza.
examples.en: I made an appointment with my wife at the doctor's.

examples.pl: Umówiłem się z szefem na podwyżkę.
examples.en: I agreed with my boss on a raise.

examples.pl: Umówiłem się ze sprzedawcą o cenę.
examples.en: I agreed with the seller on the price.

examples.pl: Umówiłem się z bratem, że pomoże mi w przeprowadzce.
examples.en: I agreed with my brother that he'll help me move.

examples.pl: Umówiłem się z kolegą, żeby zachować to w tajemnicy.
examples.en: I agreed with my friend to keep it secret.

examples.pl: Umówiłem się z zespołem, kto za co odpowiada.
examples.en: I agreed with the team who's responsible for what.

bindingConstraints.text: Label do/na targets as realizations, retain direct content clauses, and do not encode w sprawie + Genitive as a governed construction.

meanings.internalScope: Making telephone contact with a person or institution and optionally reporting or requesting content (WSJP sense 3). do + Genitive and na + Accusative are documented narrowed realizations of the generalized DOKĄD call-target role, never exclusive government. że and żeby introduce exact content alternatives, independent of the target rows. Call source/device, time, frequency, manner, and topic phrases such as w sprawie + Genitive are not complements — w sprawie appears only in Połączenia, never in Składnia, so it is not governed.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: Use do + Genitive for who you're calling — a documented target realization, not exclusive government: dzwonię do mamy (I'm calling my mom).
Use na + Accusative for an institution or number you're calling — another documented target realization: dzwonię na policję (I'm calling the police).
Use że to report what you're calling to say: dzwonię, że się spóźnię (I'm calling to say I'll be late).
Use żeby to request an action: dzwonię, żebyś odebrał paczkę (I'm calling to ask you to pick up the package).

examples.en: I'm calling my mom.
I'm calling the police.
I'm calling to say I'll be late.
I'm calling to ask you to pick up the package.

meanings.internalScope: Spoken communication that conveys interpretable content (WSJP sense 1), with recipient and content realized through separate object, topic, clause, or direct-speech schemas — never one maximal KOMU + CO + o + że + żeby template. Dative and do + Genitive addressees are alternatives that never co-occur in one pattern, and every recipient is optional. Direct speech carries no recipient at all. Voice, manner, channel, location, time, and communicative circumstances are not complements. Directly listed adverbial JAK lies outside the locked four complement types and is not represented.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: What you said takes the Accusative; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you told: powiedziałem koledze prawdę (I told my friend the truth).
Use o + Locative for the topic you told someone about, which is required here; the bare Dative recipient is optional: powiedziałem koledze o problemie (I told my friend about the problem).
Use że to introduce what you said as a clause; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you told: powiedziałem koledze, że wyjeżdżam (I told my friend that I'm leaving).
Use żeby to introduce what you asked someone to do; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you told: powiedziałem koledze, żeby poczekał (I told my friend to wait).
Use a question word to introduce what you said; you can optionally add the bare Dative for who you told: powiedziałem koledze, o której wracam (I told my friend what time I'm coming back).
What you said takes the Accusative; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you told: powiedziałem do koleżanki prawdę (I told the truth to my friend).
Use o + Locative for the topic, which is required here; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you told: powiedziałem do koleżanki o problemie (I mentioned the problem to my friend).
Use że to introduce what you said as a clause; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you told: powiedziałem do koleżanki, że wyjeżdżam (I mentioned to my friend that I'm leaving).
Use żeby to introduce what you asked someone to do; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you told: powiedziałem do koleżanki, żeby poczekała (I told my friend to wait).
Use a question word to introduce what you said; you can optionally add do + Genitive for who you told: powiedziałem do koleżanki, o której wracam (I mentioned to my friend what time I'm coming back).
You can report exact spoken words directly, with no recipient in this schema: powiedziałem: „Zaraz wracam” (I said: "I'll be right back.").

examples.en: I told my friend the truth.
I told my friend about the problem.
I told my friend that I'm leaving.
I told my friend to wait.
I told my friend what time I'm coming back.
I told the truth to my friend.
I mentioned the problem to my friend.
I mentioned to my friend that I'm leaving.
I told my friend to wait.

examples.pl: Powiedziałem do koleżanki, o której wracam.
examples.en: I mentioned to my friend what time I'm coming back.
I said: "I'll be right back."

meanings.internalScope: Preparing a hot meal or dish (WSJP sense 3), separate from food itself boiling/cooking and every other gotować sense. Source gives exact (CO) + (KOMU), both positions parenthesised: one schema with an optional Accusative prepared dish/meal and an optional Dative beneficiary, faithfully authored with zero required complements per the Phase 4B5 all-optional-pattern precedent. Neither position is promoted to required. dla + Genitive appears only outside the exact schema and receives no frame credit; it is never authored.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: Both the prepared dish (Accusative) and the person it's for (Dative) are optional and can be named together or left out: gotuję obiad mamie (I'm cooking dinner for my mom).

examples.en: I'm cooking dinner for my mom.

meanings.internalScope: Booking a table, room, seat, ticket, service, or comparable reservable item for a customer/beneficiary (WSJP sense 1). Source gives CO + (KOMU) and CO + (dla KOGO): the booked item is required in both schemas, while Dative and dla + Genitive are alternative, never-cumulative optional beneficiary/customer realizations. Setting time or resources aside (sense 2) and its na + Accusative purpose and dla allocation semantics are a separate meaning and receive no Phase 4 product row here; sense 2 was inspected only as a contrast boundary.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: Name what you're booking with the Accusative; add who it's for with an optional Dative: rezerwuję stolik znajomym (I'm reserving a table for my friends).
dla + Genitive is an alternative way to name the beneficiary, never combined with the Dative form: rezerwuję pokój dla rodziców (I'm reserving a room for my parents).

examples.en: I'm reserving a table for my friends.
I'm reserving a room for my parents.

meanings.internalScope: Lexical-reflexive experiencing of joy (WSJP sense 1); się is part of the canonical lemma identity, never a complement, and nothing transfers from non-reflexive cieszyć. Source gives z KOGO/CZEGO | na CO, a separate że ZDANIE, and KIM/CZYM: four alternative cause/content schemas that are never combined into one cumulative frame. z + Genitive marks an existing/completed source or cause of joy; na + Accusative marks an anticipated occasion or object; Instrumental marks a nominal cause/object; że marks a propositional cause/content. The four are semantically distinct, not interchangeable labels for the same relation.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For an existing or already-received source of joy, use z + Genitive: cieszę się z twojego sukcesu (I'm happy about your success).
For an occasion you're looking forward to, use na + Accusative: cieszę się na wakacje (I'm looking forward to the holidays).
For a nominal cause or object of satisfaction, use the bare Instrumental: cieszę się zaufaniem zespołu (I enjoy the team's trust).
For a propositional cause, add a że clause: cieszę się, że przyjechałeś (I'm happy that you came).

examples.en: I'm happy about your success.
I'm looking forward to the holidays.
I enjoy the team's trust.
I'm happy that you came.

meanings.internalScope: Lexical-reflexive worrying or being sustainedly concerned (WSJP entry); się is part of the canonical lemma identity, never a complement. Semantically distinct from fear: expresses worry/sustained concern, not fear. Source directly gives CZYM, o KOGO/CO, że ZDANIE, and ZDANIE PYTAJNOZALEŻNE: four alternative cause/content schemas. No construction is borrowed from non-reflexive martwić or from bać się; the o + Accusative overlap with released bać się is accepted product overlap, not linguistic donation, and does not remove or hide this row — the additional Instrumental and clause inventory teach meaningful new behavior.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For the cause of your worry, use the bare Instrumental: martwię się twoim zdrowiem (I'm worried about your health).
For the person or thing you're concerned about, use o + Accusative: martwię się o egzamin (I'm worried about the exam).
For a worrying fact or possibility, add a że clause: martwię się, że się spóźnimy (I'm worried that we'll be late).
For an uncertain worrying question, add an embedded question: martwię się, jak sobie poradzimy (I'm worried about how we'll manage).

examples.en: I'm worried about your health.
I'm worried about the exam.
I'm worried that we'll be late.
I'm worried about how we'll manage.

glossesEn: consent to a proposal or action
meanings.internalScope: Lexical-reflexive consent to a proposal or action (WSJP sense 1); się is part of the canonical lemma identity, never a complement. Source gives na KOGO/CO, żeby ZDANIE, infinitive, and direct speech: four alternative content schemas, none parenthesised, none carrying a partner position. No z + Instrumental partner belongs here; that relation is exclusive to opinion-agreement. Kept strictly separate from opinion/interpersonal agreement and from matching/correspondence, which is excluded entirely.

Lexical-reflexive agreement with a person or opinion (WSJP sense 2); się is part of the canonical lemma identity, never a complement. Source gives z KIM/CZYM, optional z KIM/CZYM with a że clause, and direct speech. z + Instrumental is required as its own row and optional when attached to the że row; the direct-speech row is listed alone in the source and therefore carries no partner complement, following the source rather than analogy with the other rows. No na, infinitive, or żeby is imported from consent.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For the proposal or action you're agreeing to, use na + Accusative: zgadzam się na twoją propozycję (I agree to your proposal).
For consent expressed as letting someone do something, add a żeby clause: zgadzam się, żebyś został dłużej (I agree that you can stay longer).
For consenting to do something yourself, add a bare infinitive: zgadzam się zapłacić połowę (I agree to pay half).
Consent is often given as a short spoken reply to an offer or plan: zapytałem, czy możemy zacząć jutro. „Zgadzam się” — odpowiedział (I asked if we could start tomorrow. "I agree," he replied).
To agree with a person or their view, use z + Instrumental: zgadzam się z tobą (I agree with you).
Add a że clause for what you agree with; naming who you agree with (z + Instrumental) is optional: zgadzam się z nim, że to dobry pomysł (I agree with him that it's a good idea).

Agreement with an opinion is often a short spoken reply, with no partner named in this exact shape: powiedziałem, że film był świetny. „Zgadzam się” — dodała (I said the film was great. "I agree," she added).

examples.en: I agree to your proposal.
I agree that you can stay longer.
I agree to pay half.

examples.pl: Zapytałem, czy możemy zacząć jutro. „Zgadzam się” — odpowiedział.
examples.en: I asked if we could start tomorrow. "I agree," he replied.
I agree with you.

examples.pl: Zgadzam się z nim, że to dobry pomysł.
examples.en: I agree with him that it's a good idea.

examples.pl: Powiedziałem, że film był świetny. „Zgadzam się” — dodała.
examples.en: I said the film was great. "I agree," she added.

meanings.internalScope: Inviting a person to an event/activity, a destination/institution, or another selected place (WSJP sense 1). Source gives KOGO + na CO | do CZEGO and separately KOGO + GDZIE: the invitee is required in both, while na + Accusative (event/activity) and do + Genitive (destination/institution) are alternative, exact concrete Składnia positions, never simultaneous slots and never described as narrowed realizations or exclusive government. The separate generalized GDZIE schema is selected source evidence that receives no product row; it stays fully unconcretized — no w, u, na + Locative, or other place form may ever be derived from it.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For an event or activity, name who you're inviting (Accusative) and what to (na + Accusative): zapraszam cię na urodziny (I'm inviting you to my birthday party).
For a destination or institution, use do + Genitive instead: zapraszam cię do domu (I'm inviting you to my house).

examples.en: I'm inviting you to my birthday party.
I'm inviting you to my house.

phase3Evidence.primarySourceLocator: sense 1; Definicja, Połączenia, Składnia, Informacja normatywna

meanings.internalScope: Directing or instructing someone to act (WSJP sense 1). Source gives optional Dative addressee with infinitive, żeby, direct speech, or CO, the optional Dative distributing over all four content alternatives; its normative note states the Accusative position is ordinarily a gerund/action noun, a lexical-semantic fact the locked schema cannot encode structurally and that is carried here in internalScope and learnerExplanationEn only. The infinitive here is a command/instruction relation, never glossed as ordinary recommendation. This meaning's Accusative-object pattern (dative-accusative-action-noun) is structurally identical to recommendation's dative-accusative-recommended-item; the semantic split between an instructed action-noun and a recommended item cannot be enforced structurally and depends on this internalScope, the glosses, the learner explanation, the example, and independent review.

Recommending a person or item to a potential user/customer (WSJP sense 2), independent of directive-instruction. Source gives optional Dative recipient plus a required Accusative recommended person/item; no infinitive, żeby, or direct speech belongs here.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For an instruction to act, use a bare infinitive; naming who is instructed (Dative) is optional: lekarz poleca mi odpoczywać (the doctor tells me to rest).
A żeby clause is another way to give the same instruction: szef poleca mi, żebym przygotował raport (my boss tells me to prepare the report).
An instruction can also be quoted directly: kierownik poleca mi: „Zamknij drzwi” (the manager tells me: "Close the door.").
The Accusative names the ordered action as a noun (usually a gerund/action noun), not a recommended item: trener poleca zawodnikom rozgrzewkę (the coach orders the players to warm up).
Name the recommended person or item with the Accusative; the recipient (Dative) is optional: polecam ci tę restaurację (I recommend this restaurant to you).

examples.en: The doctor tells me to rest.

examples.pl: Szef poleca mi, żebym przygotował raport.
examples.en: My boss tells me to prepare the report.
The manager tells me: "Close the door."
The coach orders the players to warm up.
I recommend this restaurant to you.

meanings.internalScope: Non-reflexive advice sense 2, giving advice about how someone should act (WSJP sense 2), strictly independent from lexical radzić sobie: no sobie in any form and no z + Instrumental coping syntax is authored anywhere on this lemma. Source gives required KOMU + CO; required KOMU with żeby or an interrogative-dependent clause; direct speech plus required KOMU; and optional KOMU with an infinitive. Dative is required in the nominal, żeby, interrogative, and direct-speech schemas but optional in the infinitive schema alone; this asymmetry is the defining structural fact of the lemma and is never normalized in either direction.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: Name who you're advising (Dative, required) and the advice item (Accusative): radzę ci ostrożność (I advise you to be careful).
A żeby clause gives the advised action, with the advisee (Dative) still required: radzę ci, żebyś odpoczął (I advise you to rest).
An embedded question gives advice content, with the advisee (Dative) still required: radzę ci, jak rozwiązać ten problem (I advise you on how to solve this problem).
Advice can be quoted directly, with the advisee (Dative) still required: radzę ci: „Odpocznij trochę” (I advise you: "Rest a little.").
With a bare infinitive, the advisee (Dative) becomes optional, unlike every other row above: radzę ci zjeść coś przed wyjściem (I advise you to eat something before leaving).

examples.en: I advise you to be careful.
I advise you to rest.

examples.pl: Radzę ci, jak rozwiązać ten problem.
examples.en: I advise you on how to solve this problem.
I advise you: "Rest a little."

examples.pl: Radzę ci zjeść coś przed wyjściem.
examples.en: I advise you to eat something before leaving.

meanings.internalScope: Appearance/character harmony or match with a target (WSJP sense 1). Source gives exact do KOGO/CZEGO, unparenthesised. No Dative is imported from senses 4 or 5; no na + Accusative from sense 2.

Physical fit by size or shape (WSJP sense 2). Source gives optional do KOGO/CZEGO or na KOGO/CO: two alternative, all-optional single-complement target realizations, never combined into one row and never promoted to required. No Dative belongs here.

glossesEn: be typical of/appropriate for someone or something
meanings.internalScope: Being typical of or appropriate for a person or thing (WSJP sense 4). Source gives optional KOMU plus do KOGO/CZEGO: the reference target (do + Genitive) is required, the evaluator (Dative) is optional. This do + Genitive is a reference-target relation, distinct from sense 1's harmony target and sense 2's fit target despite the repeated surface form. This Dative is not the sense-5 expectation-holder and carries no subject-experiencer wording.

Satisfying someone's expectations or suiting them (WSJP sense 5). Source gives optional KOMU/CZEMU as the only listed position: one all-optional single-complement pattern. Phase 3 notes this sense is suitable for a subject-experiencer characterization, but the exact Składnia lists no subject position and the locked relationType subject-experiencer requires both subject and experiencer roles; inventing a required Nominative subject absent from the source would violate the exact-source policy and destroy this all-optional shape. This row is therefore authored as lexical-frame with the Dative role experiencer, following the released canonical zależeć precedent (dative-experiencer-na-locative, also lexical-frame with no source-listed subject); the richer subject-experiencer characterization remains a product-wording/Phase 4C fact carried here, not a structural field. Do not apply this wording to senses 1, 2, or 4.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For an appearance/character match, use do + Genitive: ten krawat pasuje do garnituru (this tie matches the suit).
For a physical fit by size/shape, do + Genitive is one optional target form: ten klucz pasuje do zamka (this key fits the lock).
na + Accusative is the alternative optional target form for a physical fit: ten pierścionek pasuje na mój palec (this ring fits my finger).
do + Genitive names what something is being compared against; adding a Dative optionally names whose judgment it is: ten kolor mi do ciebie nie pasuje (I don't think this color suits you).
Name whose expectations are or aren't satisfied with an optional Dative: ten termin mi nie pasuje (this date doesn't suit me).

examples.en: This tie matches the suit.
This key fits the lock.

examples.pl: Ten pierścionek pasuje na mój palec.
examples.en: This ring fits my finger.

examples.pl: Ten kolor mi do ciebie nie pasuje.
examples.en: I don't think this color suits you.
This date doesn't suit me.

meanings.internalScope: Objective possibility or ability to do something (WSJP sense 1). Source gives an exact infinitive in Składnia. Semantically distinct from permission despite the identical infinitive shape; the distinction is not structurally enforceable and is carried here and in the learner explanation.

Absence of prohibition or having permission to do something (WSJP sense 2). Source gives an exact infinitive in Składnia. Also owns the request/help question use (Czy mogę…?, WSJP sense 4): three independent frozen statements assign that use to this meaning as sentence-level interrogative and pragmatic packaging over the same infinitive frame, never as a distinct complement, clauseKind, or architecture type. No czy clause, question complement, or third meaning is ever authored for this sense.

patterns.learnerExplanationEn: For what you're able to do, use a bare infinitive: mogę podnieść tę walizkę (I can lift this suitcase).
For what you're allowed to do, use the same bare-infinitive shape; a permission request is just this construction asked as a question: czy mogę otworzyć okno? (may I open the window?).

examples.en: I can lift this suitcase.
May I open the window?

meanings.internalScope: Core necessity or obligation to do something (WSJP sense 1). The frozen source lists an unrestricted-subject schema and a zero-subject schema, both with a bare infinitive; personal versus impersonal realization is a sentence-level fact and creates no second complement, pattern or meaning. Excludes the separate discourse uses for advice, expectation, criticism and elliptical modal talk. No subject, impersonal or question complement is ever authored.
